record.paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
record.original_question: For a family of open billiards with a variable hole H, let h=|H|/|M| be the hole size relative to the billiard boundary phase space M, and let P(t)=μ0(Ω_t) be the survival probability at time t for an initial measure μ0. For which billiards, and in which joint limits of long time t and small hole size h, does P(t) reduce to a function only of the product h t?

evidence.quote: what is the probability P(t) = μ0(Ωt) that the particle survives until time t? How does this probability behave as a function of t, the initial measure μ0, the hole location H, its size relative to the billiard boundary h = |H|/|M|
If instead both limits are taken simultaneously so that ht is constant, the survival probability numerically appears to reach a limiting function.
Open problem 4. Scaling: For what billiards and in what limits does P(t) reduce to a function of ht for a family of billiards with variable hole size h?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Q\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a billiard table (a bounded domain with piecewise smooth boundary $\partial Q$), and let a point particle move inside $Q$ with unit speed, reflecting elastically off $\partial Q$. Let $M$ denote the boundary (collision) phase space, consisting of unit tangent vectors based at boundary points and pointing into $Q$, equipped with the standard invariant billiard measure $|\cdot|$. Fix a measurable subset $H\subset \partial Q$ ("the hole"); the particle escapes the system at the first collision whose base point lies in $H$. For $t\ge 0$ let $\Omega_t\subset M$ be the set of initial conditions whose trajectories have not yet escaped by time $t$, and for a probability measure $\mu_0$ on $M$ define the survival probability
$$P(t)=\mu_0(\Omega_t).$$
Let $h=|H|/|M|$ denote the relative hole size.

Problem. Characterize all classes of billiard tables $Q$ and all joint limits $t\to\infty$, $h\to 0$ (for instance, limits in which $ht$ is held fixed, or other prescribed coupled scalings of $h$ and $t$) for which there exists a nontrivial function $F:(0,\infty)\to[0,1]$ such that, for every admissible family of holes $H$ with $|H|/|M|=h$ and every initial measure $\mu_0$ in a specified class,
$$\lim P(t)=F(ht)$$
along the limit. Identify the function $F$, the class of initial measures, and the precise admissible scaling relation between $h$ and $t$ in each case.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of identifying the billiards and joint scaling limits in which the survival probability becomes a function of $ht$ alone is reported as an open problem in surveys on open billiards. Recent works (e.g., on stadium, spherical, lemon, and Sinai billiards) provide partial scaling results — exponential decay rates linear in $h$ for hyperbolic regimes, and power-law tails with hole-size-dependent amplitudes in mixed regimes — but no general classification of billiards and limits yielding a universal function of $ht$ is established.

status_evidence.snippet: Open problem 4. Scaling: For what billiards and in what limits does P(t) reduce to a function of ht for a family of billiards with variable hole size h?
status_evidence.claim: The scaling question is explicitly posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Survival Probability for Open Spherical Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Studies survival probability scaling with hole size in specific spherical billiards.
status_evidence.claim: Partial scaling results are known in specific geometries but not a general classification.

status_evidence.title: From Hyperbolic to Non-Hyperbolic Open Billiards: An Entropy and Scaling Law Approach
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates scaling laws across hyperbolic and non-hyperbolic regimes.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to study scaling laws, indicating the general problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Linear response for Sinai billiards with small holes
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses small-hole asymptotics for Sinai billiards.
status_evidence.claim: Small-hole limits remain an active research area without a universal $ht$-scaling theorem.
